name: Lapsed Customer Return Queue
value_proposition: Turn a stripped customer export into a consent-filtered, VIP-first winback queue with drafts locked to the owner's written offers, then check a later POS export for who returned — the owner reviews and sends, and the kit never texts, emails, or invents a discount.
persona: Owner of a salon, clinic, fitness studio, or independent retail shop who can export customers from Square, Mindbody, or a POS and has not looked at who stopped coming in after about 60 days.
problem: Repeat customers go quiet and nobody builds a list. When staff remember someone, they send a vague 'we miss you' note, sometimes to people who opted out, and they never check who actually returned.
workflow: 1. The person writes winback rules before any draft: lapse threshold (last visit before this date counts as lapsed), VIP visit floor for the last 12 months, whether one-time buyers are skipped, and a written offer list the drafts may not leave. PERSON DECIDES: the lapse date, VIP floor, one-time rule, and which offers the business will actually honor.

2. The person exports customers with last visit or purchase date, last service or item, visit count in the last 12 months, and marketing-consent / do-not-contact flags, then removes emails, phones, and addresses before paste or upload. They also open last period's contact log. PERSON DECIDES: which columns to keep. This is an export review, not a live Square, Mindbody, POS, email, or SMS connection.

3. The person checks the data settings of their AI assistant (chat history, training use, and file retention) before pasting or uploading anything. File upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings. PERSON DECIDES: whether to paste the rows as text, upload a file, or not use AI for this data at all.

4. The person pastes the Skip-Rules-First Prompt and their rules from the Lapse, VIP, and Offer Worksheet, then attaches or pastes the customer rows and the contact-log names already contacted this period.

5. AI runs SKIP RULES FIRST. It sets aside rows with no marketing consent, do-not-contact, already contacted this period per the log, last visit more recent than the lapse threshold, and one-time buyers when the owner chose to skip them. Every skip lists its reason. PERSON DECIDES: whether a skipped row should still get a personal note outside this workflow.

6. AI segments the rest: VIP if visit count meets the owner's VIP floor, otherwise occasional. It ranks VIP first, then by days since last visit. It drafts one message per queued row using only last service or item, last visit date, and an offer from the written offer list. It does not invent a discount, private detail, or deadline that is not on the offer list. PERSON DECIDES: whether each draft is accurate enough to consider.

7. AI labels CONFIRMED (from the export and rules), AI INTERPRETATION (for example that days since visit do not prove why they stopped), and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. PERSON DECIDES: whether each recommended action happens.

8. The person uses the Send Review Checklist, picks the recipient from their own list, and sends from their own email or SMS tool, or decides not to. Nothing is sent automatically. After the next POS export, the person pastes the Return Check Prompt and marks returned vs still lapsed in the contact log. PERSON DECIDES: the log outcome. The Blueprint never sends, edits, cancels, or pays.
before: Lapsed regulars disappear from the book. Staff sometimes text a person they remember, including people who asked not to be contacted, and nobody counts who came back.
after: Each cycle the owner reviews a consent-filtered queue, VIP first, with drafts that only use export fields and the written offer. A later POS export shows which queued people returned.

kit_contents.title: Lapsed Customer Winback Setup Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Step-by-step setup for one cycle. It covers writing the lapse threshold, VIP visit floor, one-time-buyer rule, and written offer list; exporting customers with last visit, last service or item, visit count, and consent flags; removing emails, phones, and addresses; opening the contact log; checking the AI tool's data settings before pasting or uploading; and the rule that this is an export review, not a live Square, Mindbody, POS, email, or SMS connection. It notes that file upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings, and that rows can be pasted as text instead.

kit_contents.title: Skip-Rules-First Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt that runs SKIP RULES FIRST, lists every skip with its reason (no marketing consent, do-not-contact, already contacted this period, last visit after the lapse date, one-time buyer when that rule is on), labels CONFIRMED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately, and forbids contacting opted-out people, inventing offers, and sending.

kit_contents.title: VIP-First Draft Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt used only after skip rules run. It segments VIP vs occasional using the owner's VIP floor, ranks VIP first then by days since last visit, drafts one message per queued row using only last service or item, last visit date, and an offer from the written offer list, and forbids inventing discounts, private details, deadlines, and sending.

kit_contents.title: Return Check Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt used after a later POS export. It compares queued names to the new last-visit dates, marks returned vs still lapsed, warns that a return is not proof the message caused it, and forbids inventing return outcomes or claiming a recovery rate.

kit_contents.title: Lapse, VIP, and Offer Worksheet
kit_contents.purpose: Browser-only form where the person sets the lapse threshold date, VIP visit floor, whether to skip one-time buyers, and the written offer list (VIP offers and occasional offers). It generates a copyable rules block to paste with the prompts. Nothing is saved to Atlas.

kit_contents.title: Contact Log Template
kit_contents.purpose: Column layout (as_of, first, last_visit, last_service, visits_12mo, segment, offer_used, action, outcome) with allowed action values skipped_no_consent, skipped_dnc, skipped_recent, skipped_one_time, skipped_already_contacted, drafted_not_sent, sent_by_owner, not_sent, allowed outcome values returned, still_lapsed, unknown, and the fictional J. Rivera drafted_not_sent then returned rows from the guided demo. Includes a Copy CSV button so the person can start their own spreadsheet.

kit_contents.title: Send Review Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Interactive, session-only checklist used before contacting anyone. It confirms that SKIP RULES FIRST ran, that no-consent and do-not-contact rows were skipped, that each CONFIRMED field matches the export row, that the draft offer appears on the written offer list, that VIP ranked above occasional, that labels are separate, that a later return will not be treated as proof the message caused it, and that the person will send from their own tool themselves.

kit_contents.title: Fictional Sample Customer Export
kit_contents.purpose: The same fictional eight-row customer CSV, contact-log note, written offers, and later return-check rows used in the guided demo, labelled as fictional, with a Copy CSV button. The person can practice the full workflow in their AI tool before using real customer data.

kit_contents.title: Data and Safety Guidance
kit_contents.purpose: Rules for handling customer exports in AI tools: review data settings, remove emails and phones, do not paste passwords or card numbers, do not contact someone without marketing consent or with do-not-contact set, do not invent a discount outside the offer list, do not treat a return as proof the message caused it, and do not send the draft. It also states that file upload support differs by plan and that nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically.

decision_rules: Write SKIP RULES FIRST and apply it before any segment, rank, or draft.
Skip any row whose marketing_consent is no or missing. Show the reason 'marketing_consent is no' or 'marketing_consent missing'.
Skip any row whose do_not_contact is yes. Show the reason 'do_not_contact is yes'.
Skip any row already contacted this period per the contact log. Show the reason 'already contacted this period'.
Skip any row whose last_visit is on or after the owner's lapse_if_last_visit_before date. Show the reason and the exact sentence 'Do not queue someone whose last visit is after your lapse date.'.
If the owner set skip_one_time_buyers, skip any row with visits_12mo equal to 1. Show the reason 'one-time buyer'.
If a remaining row is missing last_visit, last_service, visits_12mo, or marketing_consent, do not draft it. List it under NEEDS YOUR CHECK.
Segment remaining rows as VIP when visits_12mo meets the owner's VIP floor; otherwise occasional.
Rank VIP rows before occasional rows. Within a segment, rank by days since last visit (highest first), calculated from as_of minus last_visit.

Draft only from last_service or last item, last_visit date, and an offer that appears on the owner's written offer list for that segment. Do not invent a discount, private detail, deadline, or recovery rate.
VIP drafts may use only VIP offers. Occasional drafts may use only occasional offers.
Days since visit do not prove why the person stopped coming. That guess is AI INTERPRETATION, not a CONFIRMED fact.
On a later POS export, mark queued people RETURNED when last_visit moved after the prior as_of, otherwise still lapsed. A return is not proof the message caused it.
The draft is a draft only. Do not send it. Do not edit the POS. Suggest a contact-log row; the person adds it.
On a later cycle, start from a new export and the current contact log. Do not reuse a prior draft as if it were sent.
human_ai_boundary: AI applies the skip rules the owner wrote. The person writes the lapse date, VIP floor, one-time rule, and offer list, and holds the real consent record.
AI lists every skip with a reason. The person decides whether a skipped row still gets a personal note outside this workflow.
AI segments VIP vs occasional and ranks the queue. The person decides whether that ranking matches how they value regulars.
AI drafts only from export fields and the written offer list. The person checks each draft against the export and the offers they will honor.
AI never chooses or sees the recipient email or phone. The person addresses and sends every message from their own email or SMS tool, or decides not to.
AI marks returned vs still lapsed only when the person pastes a later export. The person records the log outcome and does not treat a return as proof the message caused it.
The person decides whether any recommended action happens.
safety: Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically. Every page states that the person sends it, and that nothing is sent automatically.
Atlas does not connect to Square, Mindbody, a POS, email, SMS, or any other vendor. It has no OAuth flow, no API call, and does not upload the person's data to any third party.

Before pasting or uploading exports to an AI tool, the person is told to review that tool's data settings (such as chat history, training use, and file retention) and to remove emails, phones, addresses, and other columns the workflow does not need.
The kit tells the person not to paste phone numbers, email addresses, account passwords, or payment card numbers into the AI tool.
File upload support and data controls in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini differ by plan, account, and admin settings. The kit says so and does not claim any plan includes a specific capability.

The kit tells the person not to contact someone without marketing consent, not to contact do-not-contact rows, not to invent a discount outside the offer list, and not to treat a return as proof the message caused it.
The kit tells the person that a missing consent column is their risk: without it, skip rules cannot protect opted-out people.
All demo and sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional on the page.
Worksheet entries and checklist progress stay in the browser session only and are not saved to Atlas.

The pages contain no recovery-rate claims, savings claims, ROI claims, prices, or checkout. The fictional offer-list phrase '10% off next color' may appear only as an owner-written offer in the demo and sample data, not as a claimed result.
required_data_tools: POS, booking, or customer-list export (CSV) with last visit date, last item or service, visit count, and consent flags
Owner-set lapse threshold and VIP visit floor
Written offer list (only offers the business will actually honor)
Contact log spreadsheet (template in the kit)
The owner's own email or SMS tool
A file-capable AI assistant. File upload support differs by plan, account, and admin settings; rows can be pasted as text instead.

constraints: Private preview only. The guided demo lives at /blueprints/inactive-customer-winback and the Premium kit at /blueprints/inactive-customer-winback/kit. Both pages set robots noindex and are not linked from the homepage, header navigation, or the sitemap.

The Premium kit requires requireUser from src/lib/auth.ts and hasActiveEntitlement for this product. It is labelled "Premium · Private preview". It shows no Stripe price, checkout, or Buy Premium unless the product is already in PAID_PRODUCTS.
All sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional. No live connector, OAuth flow, API call, or upload to a third party.
AI prepares; the person decides. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled separately. Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically.
No invented statistics, savings, or ROI claims. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini capabilities differ by plan; say so where it matters.

Product files live in app/blueprints/inactive-customer-winback/, components/premium/inactive-customer-winback/, and src/lib/premium/inactive-customer-winback/. Register the Blueprint in src/lib/blueprints.ts. Do not edit Daily Inbox, Collections product behavior, Stripe, or Production.
e2e/inactive-customer-winback/authenticated.spec.ts is read-only once it exists. Do not skip, weaken, or rewrite it. Authenticated QA uses automatic session refresh.
Keyboard accessible, visible labels, no horizontal scrolling at a phone-sized viewport, no console errors.
